biological.citation: Chen et al. 2022 - Deleterious Variation in BR Serine/Threonine Kinase 2 Classified a Subtype of Autism (PMID: 35754711)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9 brsk2b-deficient zebrafish showed higher embryonic mortality, developmental delay, reduced activity, increased anxiety and reduced social interaction (ASD-like behaviors). Brain mRNA for homer1b, mbpa, mpz and plp1b was increased and isl1a was decreased. A proband with a de novo BRSK2 p.R222X nonsense variant had typical ASD behaviors.

biological.citation: Hiatt et al. 2019 - Deleterious Variation in BRSK2 Associates with a Neurodevelopmental Disorder (PMID: 30879638)
biological.summary: Nine DD/ID probands carried rare heterozygous BRSK2 variants (six predicted loss-of-function, three damaging missense), all absent from variant databases and de novo in all six probands with parental data. De novo variation was enriched over background mutation rate, and BRSK2 is intolerant to protein-altering variation.

biological.citation: Further characterization of the BRSK2-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 42509346)
biological.summary: In Drosophila, pan-neuronal knockdown of the BRSK2 orthologue sff caused impaired locomotion and seizure susceptibility. Overexpressing human wild-type BRSK2 was toxic (lethal or locomotor impairment). Most kinase-domain and KA1 missense variants showed partial loss of function, while a few variants showed possible gain of function. The study also describes 52 patients with heterozygous BRSK2 variants.

biological.citation: Jab1 interacts with brain-specific kinase 2 (BRSK2) and promotes its degradation in the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway (PMID: 22609399)
biological.summary: Jab1 directly interacts with BRSK2 (GST pull-down and immunoprecipitation) and co-localizes with it in the perinuclear region. Jab1 promotes BRSK2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, and Jab1 silencing raises BRSK2 levels. Exogenous Jab1 reverses BRSK2-induced G2/M arrest.

biological.citation: APC/C(Cdh1) targets brain-specific kinase 2 (BRSK2) for degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway (PMID: 23029325)
biological.summary: BRSK2 localizes to centrosomes in mitosis, and its levels peak in mitosis and fall in G1. APC/C-Cdh1 degrades BRSK2 through its KEN box. BRSK2 overexpression increases the G2/M fraction, placing BRSK2 in cell-cycle control.

biological.citation: BRSK2 induced by nutrient deprivation promotes Akt activity in pancreatic cancer via downregulation of mTOR activity (PMID: 28591720)
biological.summary: Nutrient deprivation induces BRSK2 in PDAC cells. BRSK2 phosphorylates TSC2 and suppresses mTORC1, which relieves mTORC1 feedback inhibition of Akt and enhances cell survival.

biological.citation: Gain-of-function genetic screen of the kinome reveals BRSK2 as an inhibitor of the NRF2 transcription factor (PMID: 32546533)
biological.summary: A kinome gain-of-function screen found that BRSK2 and BRSK1 suppress NRF2 transcription and protein levels in a kinase-activity-dependent manner. Phosphoproteomics and RNAseq showed BRSK2 drives AMPKα2 signaling and suppresses mTOR, reducing global protein synthesis.

biological.citation: BRSK2 in pancreatic β cells promotes hyperinsulinemia-coupled insulin resistance and its genetic variants are associated with human type 2 diabetes (PMID: 37188647)
biological.summary: BRSK2 genetic variants are associated with worse glucose metabolism, hyperinsulinemia and insulin resistance in a Chinese population. BRSK2 protein is elevated in β cells of T2DM patients and HFD-fed mice. β-cell Brsk2 knockout protects against HFD-induced hyperinsulinemia, obesity and insulin resistance, whereas gain of function causes hyperglycemia. BRSK2 senses lipid signals and drives basal insulin secretion in a kinase-dependent manner.

biological.citation: Brain-selective kinase 2 (BRSK2) phosphorylation on PCTAIRE1 negatively regulates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic β-cells (PMID: 22798068)
biological.summary: BRSK2 is abundant in pancreatic islets and MIN6 cells. It interacts with PCTAIRE1 (yeast two-hybrid, pull-down, co-IP) and phosphorylates it at Ser-12, which reduces glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. BRSK2 siRNA raises serum insulin in mice.

biological.citation: BRSK2 plays a role in autophagy and cancer cell growth and survival under nutrient deprivation stress via the PIK3C3 pathway (PMID: 41258112)
biological.summary: BRSK2 is overexpressed in aggressive breast cancer and associated with reduced disease-specific survival. It regulates basal autophagy, activates AKT, STAT3 and NF-κB, and associates with the Vps34-PI3K class III-Beclin-1-ATG14 complexes. BRSK2 knockdown or inhibition with GW296115 reduced autophagy, growth and metastatic potential, and increased apoptosis.
